title: Grove's compensation is indexed to both the Base Rate and deposit volume, so Sky's cost auto-scales with monetary policy
content:
A.2.8.2.10.2.1.2 sets Grove's ongoing compensation as `Chronicle_Point_Reward_Instance_USDS_Deposited x 20% x Base_Rate`, where the Base Rate is Sky's governance-set rate from A.3.1.2.1. The stated justification is that it "recognizes Grove's role in promoting and supporting Chronicle across integrations within the Sky Ecosystem."

Structurally this is a revenue share, not a fee. Both inputs float: deposit volume floats with adoption, and the Base Rate floats with Sky's monetary policy. The 20% is the only negotiated constant.

That design has a real advantage — the Accord never needs amending when conditions change, which matters given that amendment requires an Atlas Edit. It also aligns Grove with growth in Chronicle-integrated deposits.

The cost is that Grove's income is exposed to a variable Sky itself controls. When governance cuts the Base Rate for stability reasons, Grove's compensation falls proportionally with no reference to the work it performed that month. Indexing a service fee to a policy lever means the service provider bears policy risk, which is a different bargain from bearing adoption risk alone.
description: Deposits in the Chronicle Point Reward Instance x 20% x Base Rate: a fee expressed as a share of yield rather than a fixed amount, which needs no renegotiation when rates or TVL move.
